title: There is no men like me, only me
subtitle: A collection of letters
ending: Be the change you want to see in the world

body: Today was an ordinary day, though somehow it felt heavier than most. The sky remained where it always is, the roads carried people to places they needed to be, and time continued its quiet journey without asking anyone's permission.

In the afternoon, sunlight rested on my window for a while. It wasn't particularly beautiful, yet it seemed important enough to notice. Perhaps some things attract our attention not because they mean something, but because they remind us that meaning exists somewhere.

I found myself thinking about memories. Not any memory in particular, just the strange way they arrive uninvited and leave before we can fully understand them. Sometimes they feel closer than reality, and sometimes they seem like stories that happened to someone else.

The evening came slowly. The city became quieter, though not truly quiet. There were still lights in distant buildings and sounds from streets I couldn't see. It made me wonder how many people spend their nights thinking about things they will never say out loud.
I don't think this letter is about anything specific. Perhaps that is why I kept writing it. Some thoughts are too small to become conversations and too large to disappear completely.
So I leave these words here, carrying many feelings and explaining none of them.
